title: Dominant-negative HCN2 does not rescue nicotine brain defects

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Dominant-negative HCN2 does not rescue nicotine brain defects

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos injected with a dominant-negative, non-conducting HCN2 mutant showed no rescue of brain morphology defects (about 70% defective), so the rescue depends on HCN2 channel conductance.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 rescues nicotine exposure-induced brain defects

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In contrast, nicotine-exposed embryos injected with a mutant, dominant-negative form of HCN2 failed to show rescue of brain morphology defects (~70%) (Fig. 5f).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Results › HCN2 rescues nicotine exposure-induced brain defects”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos exposed to nicotine (0.1 mg/mL, stages 10–35), injected with Hcn2-DN (GYG→AAA pore mutant) mRNA

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-12: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The negative-control comparison is clear and informative about conductance, though expression and off-target effects remain. The particular matched perturbation data appear confined to the reported experiment, so an independent resolution likely needs new observations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare blinded brain-defect rates in nicotine-treated embryos receiving wild-type HCN2, dominant-negative HCN2, or injection control, and test whether rescue occurs only with the conducting channel.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No open embryo-level defect dataset is identified.

Dominant-negative expression may differ from wild-type expression.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Wild-type versus pore-mutant under nicotine is a clear conductance test. The published contrast is a summary percentage in one figure, with supporting electrophysiology only in the supplement's traces. No open dataset records expression-matched defect calls. Until those calls or a replication exist, the dependence on conductance cannot be reanalyzed.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Under the same nicotine regimen, compare major brain-defect incidence after Hcn2-DN (GYG to AAA) mRNA with the wild-type HCN2 rescue arm. Conductance dependence is confirmed if the DN arm stays near 70% defective while wild-type HCN2 returns to control; rescue by the DN construct would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The pore mutant must be shown to lack current in the embryo, not only in a heterologous cell.

Unequal protein level could mimic a conductance requirement.

DN and wild-type morphology counts are not in a public table.
